chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the slave who marries a free woman, then is freed, and then commits immorality: so he said: 'There is no stoning upon him until he has intercourse with the free woman after he has been emancipated.' I said, 'Does the free woman have a right of choice over him when he is emancipated?' He said, 'No. She has already consented to him while he was a slave, so he remains upon his first marriage.'

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning; the hadd punishment for zina (fornication/adultery) applied to muhsan individuals
key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: free woman; a woman of full legal capacity, not enslaved
key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: right of option/choice; in family law, the right to void or maintain a marriage contract
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: slave (male); a legally owned person with restricted legal capacity in Islamic law
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٌ: owned/slave; one whose legal capacity is restricted by ownership

ai.seo_question: Does a slave who commits adultery after being freed receive the stoning penalty according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the legal status of a man who was enslaved when he contracted a marriage with a free woman and subsequently gained his freedom. In classical Islamic jurisprudence, the hadd punishment of stoning (rajm) for adultery is applicable only to a muhsan individual — one who is free, has been validly married, and has consummated that marriage as a free person. The Imam rules that a slave-turned-freedman does not incur the stoning penalty for any illicit act committed before that consummation occurs as a free man, as the condition of ihsan was not yet met. He also clarifies that the free wife retains no right of option (khiyar) to void the marriage upon his emancipation, since she entered the marriage with full knowledge of his enslaved status.
